描述_EN: the inscription, situated on the back of the tile, would have been visible from the back of the temple, once the tile had been attached to the uppermost point of the roof. the architectural ornament has two large grooves on the sides of the plaque to secure it into position while the figure represents wei tuo, a buddhist deity commonly depicted as a warrior. to fund such an ornate buddhist ornament donations would have been received from the local monastic community. during the ming dynasty (1368-1644) tile production flourished. this fine example of the tilemaker's art, modelled with a standing figure in high relief, was designed for the main centre-piece on the roof ridge of a buddhist temple. kiln centres in china's northern provinces - hebei, for example - have been producing tiles from the 6th century to the present day.
描述_ZN: 碑文位于瓦片的背面，一旦瓦片被固定在屋顶的最上方，从寺庙的背面就可以看到。 建筑装饰品的两侧有两个大的凹槽，以固定它的位置，而人物代表韦陀，一个通常被描绘为战士的佛教神。 为了资助这样一个华丽的佛教装饰品，当地的僧侣们都会捐款。 在明朝（1368-1644）时期，瓦片生产蓬勃发展。 这是瓦匠艺术的一个很好的例子，以高浮雕的方式塑造了一个站立的人物，被设计为佛教寺庙屋脊上的主要中心部件。 中国北方省份的窑洞中心--例如河北--从6世纪到今天一直在生产瓦片。
